items.text: Society's moral rules apply to me:

options.A: Fully—I should follow them like everyone else
options.C: Generally—but my situation may justify exceptions
options.D: Selectively—I follow those that make sense to me
options.E: Optionally—I decide which rules merit my compliance

items.text: You know you'll never be caught breaking a rule that most people follow. Does the rule still bind you?

options.A: Yes—moral rules apply regardless of detection
options.B: Yes—my integrity matters even when unobserved
options.C: Probably—though consequences do factor into morality
options.D: Depends—some rules only matter because of social enforcement
options.E: Not necessarily—undetected rule-breaking may be rational

items.text: Following society's moral rules matters even when no one is watching because:

options.A: Moral obligations are objectively real regardless of observation
options.B: Character and integrity are developed through consistent action
options.C: Rules generally serve good purposes worth honoring
options.D: Social fabric depends on general compliance
options.E: Actually, it only matters pragmatically when detection is possible

interpretation.-2: Social moral rules fully apply to me
